Row 1. Sc-lint docs say pub items stay checked, so the sc-lint team must choose: exempt (S1 transitively) or keep reporting. Not a parity gap.
Rand ruling (relayed by team-lead 2026-10-30): "S8 = EXEMPT pub POSIX-only helpers"
Conflict question (team-lead, 2026-10-30): "ANC-015 against ANC-017. ANC-015 says to report any `cfg(unix)` item with no portable counterpart. ANC-017 says to exempt public POSIX-only helpers that have no Windows counterpart. They overlap" Rand (2026-10-30): "we must have an approved exception path to knowingly opt out."
anchors.context: Phase M planning; #786 S8 text, Rand's S8 ruling and his ruling on the ANC-015/ANC-017 conflict, relayed by team-lead 2026-10-30
anchors.summary: [pending definition: approved exception path] #786 S8: pub POSIX-only helpers exempt via approved exception
anchors.scope: The item changes PORT-010 handling of pub items, helper exemptions or exception declarations in crates/sc-lint-portability.

fail: Adds a built-in PORT-010 rule that skips every pub cfg(unix) helper with no Windows counterpart, with no exception declaration.

anchors.statement: By default, sc-lint must run sc_lint.* wheel helper steps on the sc-lint kit's own venv interpreter (.sc-lint/venv), even when [tool.sc-lint].runner.python is set.
anchors.quote:
plain `python` steps use `runner.python`; `sc_lint.*` wheel helpers always use the kit interpreter and `runner.python` must never apply to them.
Conflict question (team-lead, 2026-10-30): "GH-198.runner-argv against GH-198.kit-helpers. The literal rule \"a leading `python` becomes the `runner.python` interpreter\" would also rewrite `python -m sc_lint.*`. The kit-helpers record says those always use the kit interpreter, never overridden." Rand (2026-10-30): "a consumer must have a method to override behavior."
anchors.context: Phase M planning; #198 issue text (https://github.com/randlee/sc-lint/issues/198#issuecomment-6513016954 (b)) plus Rand's ruling on the runner-argv/kit-helpers conflict, relayed by team-lead 2026-10-30
anchors.summary: #198: sc_lint.* helpers default to the kit interpreter
anchors.scope: The item adds or changes how sc_lint.* helper steps (deny, manifests, shear, spell) are run in crates/sc-lint.
anchors.deterministic_check: A runner test with runner.python set and no consumer override shows an sc_lint.lint_cargo_deny step resolves to the kit venv interpreter.

pass: With no consumer override, sc_lint.* wheel helper steps run on the kit interpreter even when runner.python is set. Evidence: test kit_helpers_ignore_runner_python passes, showing sc_lint.lint_cargo_deny resolves to the kit venv with runner.python set.
fail: Applies runner.python to every step, including sc_lint.lint_cargo_deny.

anchors.statement: sc-lint's dependency ownership check (global_dependency_ownership) must limit enforcement to source files only when a consumer opts in through a setting, and otherwise keep checking all files.
anchors.quote:
sc-lint enforces dependency ownership on source files only, and we know which of atm-core's three boundary settings it already covers.
Definition question (team-lead, 2026-10-30): "is source-only enforcement the default behavior, or an opt-in setting?" Rand: "opt-in"
anchors.context: Phase M planning; Rand approved the sentence and answered 'opt-in' to the definition question, relayed by team-lead 2026-10-30 (lint-xccm)
anchors.summary: #136: opt-in source-only dependency ownership
anchors.scope: The item changes global_dependency_ownership or SCB-MANIFEST-004 in crates/sc-lint-boundary, or their config keys.
anchors.deterministic_check: A boundary test shows that, with the source-only setting on, an ownership violation in src/ is reported and the same import in a tests/ target is not; with the setting off, both are reported.

pass: Adds an opt-in source-only dependency ownership setting; with it on, src/ is checked and tests/ is not, and with it off every file is still checked. Evidence: test ownership_source_only passes, showing a tests/ import is reported only when the setting is off.
fail: Dependency ownership keeps checking every file, including tests/, and offers no way to limit it to source files.
Makes source-only the new default, so tests/ files stop being checked for every consumer without any setting.
